cycles.red: the standalone package had no isolated Audit login, no non-login wrapper owner and no explicit activation entrypoint
cycles.green: the initializer creates both roles as NOLOGIN/NOINHERIT/NOBYPASSRLS, migration 123 installs the closed graph and the packaged CLI performs the only explicit activation

cycles.red: transferring wrapper ownership caused the invoker trigger to misclassify the exact target definer and reject a valid Rust append
cycles.green: the guard trusts only the exact no-login Audit store owner for target provenance while direct, inherited and SET ROLE legacy identities remain denied

cycles.red: independent adversarial review found memberships, default ACLs, grant options, alternate grantors and object-owner drift that the first role graph did not reject
cycles.green: activation now checks exact role flags, membership, ownership, RLS, direct ACL grantor, grantability, database/schema scope, default ACLs, definers, columns, sequences and large objects before LOGIN

cycles.red: role and database defaults could install ambient tenant or RLS-bypass settings before a Rust transaction
cycles.green: both dedicated roles must have empty rolconfig, no role/database settings and no cluster/database ambient setting row accepted by activation

cycles.red: a PG14-only public-schema owner assumption would reject PG15+ fresh databases and PG15+ parameter ACLs could grant trigger-disabling authority
cycles.green: the graph accepts pg_database_owner only under an opc_admin-owned database and dynamically rejects PUBLIC/runtime/owner SET or ALTER SYSTEM parameter ACLs on PG15+; actual PG16 physical validation remains not_run

cycles.red: an extra trigger or rewrite rule on a target table could execute inside the wrapper owner's authority without appearing in runtime function ACL checks
cycles.green: the event table must have exactly the reviewed legacy and immutable triggers, the head must have none and both targets must have zero rewrite rules; physical extra-trigger and extra-rule attacks are rejected

cycles.red: session_replication_role=replica could disable ordinary trigger fences even with a closed function and parameter ACL graph
cycles.green: migration and activation require both current and reset session_replication_role to be origin; the physical replica-session attack is rejected

cycles.red: effective PUBLIC USAGE could conceal a missing dedicated schema grant and the first activation checks did not bind every allowed ACL entry to the object owner grantor
cycles.green: both dedicated roles require one exact direct public-schema USAGE grant and all table, database and schema ACL entries bind the expected owner grantor; physical revoke and alternate-grantor attacks are rejected
